## 2.4 Implementation Considerations

This section addresses technical constraints, performance requirements, scalability considerations, security implications, and maintenance requirements across all features.

### 2.4.1 Technical Constraints

#### 2.4.1.1 Platform Constraints

**Mainframe Platform Requirements**:
- z/OS operating system with CICS Transaction Server and batch initiator subsystems
- IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS compiler (version requirements per installation)
- VSAM dataset management with adequate DASD (Direct Access Storage Device) allocations
- 3270 terminal emulator for user interface access
- JES2 or JES3 job entry subsystem for batch job management

**Data Storage Limitations**:
- VSAM-only data persistence (no relational database in Version 1)
- Fixed-length record structures (no variable-length or compressed records)
- KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set) limited by key size and record length
- Sequential files for daily feeds and reject processing
- GDG (Generation Data Group) management for statement archival

**Processing Model Constraints**:
- Synchronous online transaction processing (no asynchronous messaging in Version 1)
- Pseudo-conversational CICS programming (no conversational mode)
- Batch processing limited to sequential job execution
- No parallel processing or multi-threading

#### 2.4.1.2 Encoding and Character Set

**EBCDIC on Mainframe**:
- All mainframe data stored in EBCDIC (Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code)
- Test data files provided in ASCII format require conversion
- Character comparison and sorting follow EBCDIC collation sequence
- No Unicode support, limited to single-byte character sets

**Data Conversion Requirements**:
- ASCII test data converted to EBCDIC during file loading
- Numeric data requires proper zone and pack conversion
- Date and time fields require format standardization (CCYYMMDD, ISO-8601)

#### 2.4.1.3 Transaction Volume Limitations

**Online Processing**:
- CICS region size constrains concurrent user capacity
- Pseudo-conversational design optimizes resource utilization
- No explicit transaction rate limiting in Version 1
- File contention possible under high concurrent access

**Batch Processing**:
- Daily transaction feed processing: target 10,000 transactions per hour
- Statement generation: target 10,000 statements per hour
- Interest calculation: process all accounts within monthly batch window
- Sequential processing pattern limits throughput

### 2.4.2 Performance Requirements

#### 2.4.2.1 Online Response Time Targets

| Function Category | Target Response Time | Measurement Point |
|-------------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Authentication (F-001) | ≤ 2 seconds | Enter key to menu display |
| Account View (F-003) | ≤ 2 seconds | Account ID entry to detail display |
| Account Update (F-003) | ≤ 2 seconds | Submit to confirmation |
| Card List (F-004) | ≤ 3 seconds | Initial list display |
| Card Paging (F-004) | ≤ 1 second | PF7/PF8 to next page |
| Transaction Entry (F-005) | ≤ 3 seconds | Submit to confirmation |
| Transaction List (F-005) | ≤ 3 seconds | Initial list display |
| Bill Payment (F-006) | ≤ 3 seconds | Submit to confirmation |
| Report Request (F-007) | ≤ 2 seconds | Submit to TDQ confirmation |

**Performance Optimization Techniques**:
- Direct key access for single-record retrieval (O(1) operations)
- VSAM browse operations for list displays (positioned sequential reads)
- COMMAREA eliminates session state file I/O
- Field-level validation before file operations

#### 2.4.2.2 Batch Processing Targets

| Batch Job | Target Throughput | Measurement |
|-----------|------------------|-------------|
| Daily Transaction Posting (F-005) | 10,000 transactions/hour | CBTRN02C processing rate |
| Interest Calculation (F-008) | All accounts in 2 hours | CBACT04C monthly job |
| Statement Generation (F-007) | 10,000 statements/hour | CBSTM03A processing rate |
| Master File Initialization (F-009) | Complete in 10 minutes | All initialization jobs |

**Batch Optimization Techniques**:
- Sequential reads for feed file processing (optimized I/O)
- Centralized I/O subroutine (CBSTM03B) reduces file operations
- Buffer sizing for file I/O (configurable via JCL)
- Random access pattern for balance updates (indexed by account ID)

#### 2.4.2.3 File Access Performance

**VSAM KSDS Performance Characteristics**:
- Direct key access: O(log n) complexity via B-tree index
- Sequential browse: Near-linear performance for ordered reads
- Alternate index: Additional overhead for index maintenance
- Update operations: Read-modify-write pattern with exclusive control

**File I/O Bottleneck Mitigation**:
- Appropriate buffer allocations (BUFND, BUFNI parameters)
- Control interval sizing for record access patterns
- Free space allocation for insert-intensive files
- Periodic reorganization for fragmented datasets

### 2.4.3 Scalability Considerations

#### 2.4.3.1 Vertical Scaling Limitations

**CICS Region Constraints**:
- CICS region size (DSA, EDSA, ECDSA) limits concurrent transactions
- Maximum threads constrained by MAXTASK parameter
- Transaction class definitions partition workload
- Storage violations cause region abends (degraded service)

**File Size Limitations**:
- VSAM dataset size limited by DASD volume capacity
- Large datasets require additional volumes (multi-volume datasets)
- Index size grows with record count (B-tree depth increases)
- Browse operations slower on large datasets

#### 2.4.3.2 Horizontal Scaling Limitations

**No Distribution in Version 1**:
- Single CICS region (no multi-region support)
- No workload balancing across regions
- No database connection pooling (VSAM is local)
- Batch jobs execute serially (no parallel job streams)

**Future Scalability Enhancements**:
- CICS region partitioning by function (e.g., separate inquiry and update regions)
- Database migration (Db2 supports connection pooling, parallel access)
- Batch parallelization (split transaction feed by account range)
- Asynchronous processing via message queues (MQ integration in Version 2)

#### 2.4.3.3 Pagination and List Management

**Online List Pagination**:
- Card list: 7 cards per page (F-004)
- Transaction list: 10 transactions per page (F-005)
- User list: 10 users per page (F-002)
- Browse position maintained in COMMAREA or temporary storage
- Forward/backward paging via PF7/PF8 keys

**Pagination Performance**:
- Forward paging: READNEXT operations (efficient)
- Backward paging: READPREV operations or re-establish browse position (less efficient)
- Large skip distances (e.g., page 1 to page 100) require sequential reads

### 2.4.4 Security Implications

#### 2.4.4.1 Authentication Weaknesses

**Clear Text Passwords**:
- Passwords stored in SEC-USR-PWD field without encryption or hashing
- COSGN00C performs direct string comparison
- Not suitable for production deployment
- Mitigation: Implement password hashing (SHA-256, bcrypt) in production environments

**Session Management Risks**:
- COMMAREA contains user ID and role in plain text
- No session timeout mechanism implemented
- Session hijacking possible if terminal left unattended
- Mitigation: Implement session timeout, terminal lock features

**No Multi-Factor Authentication**:
- Single-factor authentication (password only)
- No SMS codes, tokens, or biometric authentication
- Mitigation: Integrate with enterprise MFA solution for production

#### 2.4.4.2 Authorization Gaps

**Coarse-Grained Role-Based Access**:
- Two roles only: Admin ('A') and User ('U')
- No fine-grained permissions (e.g., read-only account access)
- All regular users have same privileges
- Mitigation: Implement attribute-based access control (ABAC) for production

**No Audit Logging**:
- User actions not logged to audit trail
- No transaction audit records
- File access not tracked
- Mitigation: Implement comprehensive audit logging, SIEM integration

#### 2.4.4.3 Data Protection Deficiencies

**Sensitive Data Exposure**:
- PII fields: SSN (CUST-SSN), government ID (CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID)
- PCI data: Full card number (CARD-NUM), CVV (CARD-CVV-CD)
- No encryption at rest or in transit
- No data masking on displays
- Mitigation: Implement field-level encryption, display masking, PCI DSS compliance controls

**No RACF Integration**:
- Application-level security only
- VSAM files not protected by RACF profiles
- No external security manager integration
- Mitigation: Integrate with RACF or external security manager (e.g., CA Top Secret, ACF2)

#### 2.4.4.4 Compliance Considerations

**PCI-DSS Non-Compliance**:
- Full card number displayed and stored without truncation
- CVV stored in CARDFILE (PCI-DSS prohibits CVV storage)
- No encryption, tokenization, or masking
- No network segmentation or firewall rules
- Mitigation: Full PCI-DSS remediation required for production credit card processing

**Regulatory Reporting**:
- No compliance reporting (TILA, FCRA, BSA, AML)
- No credit bureau reporting interfaces
- No tax reporting (1099-INT, 1099-C)
- Mitigation: Implement regulatory reporting interfaces for production

### 2.4.5 Maintenance Requirements

#### 2.4.5.1 Copybook Synchronization

**Change Management Process**:
- Copybook changes require coordinated recompilation of all dependent programs
- No automated dependency tracking in Version 1
- Manual identification of impacted programs
- Risk of out-of-sync data structures if recompilation incomplete

**Copybook Versioning**:
- No version control within copybook definitions
- COBOL REPLACING clause can mitigate field name changes
- Record length changes break compatibility with existing data files
- Mitigation: Implement copybook version registry, automated dependency analysis

#### 2.4.5.2 BMS Map Maintenance

**Map Translation and Installation**:
- BMS map source changes require assembly/translation
- Physical and symbolic map copybooks generated
- CICS program requires NEWCOPY command to load updated maps
- Incomplete installation causes map-program mismatch errors

**Screen Redesign Constraints**:
- 24x80 character grid constraint limits redesign options
- Field positioning changes require program logic updates
- No dynamic screen rendering (all layouts compile-time)
- Mitigation: Consider web or mobile UI replacement for modern user experience

#### 2.4.5.3 Test Data Management

**Test Data Refresh**:
- Test data files in app/data/ASCII directory (fixed-width format)
- Manual updates required for data changes
- File format contracts must be byte-exact
- No automated test data generation

**Data File Inventory**:
- acctdata.txt: 50 account records (300 bytes each)
- carddata.txt: 50 card records (150 bytes)
- cardxref.txt: 50 cross-reference records (34 bytes, fully numeric)
- custdata.txt: 50 customer records (500 bytes)
- dailytran.txt: Daily transaction feed (350 bytes per record)
- discgrp.txt: 3 disclosure group blocks
- tcatbal.txt: 50 transaction category balance records
- trancatg.txt: 18 transaction category definitions
- trantype.txt: 7 transaction type codes

**Test Data Limitations**:
- Small dataset (50 records) insufficient for performance testing
- No negative test cases (invalid data scenarios)
- No boundary condition testing data
- Mitigation: Expand test data with synthetic data generation tools

#### 2.4.5.4 Batch Job Sequencing

**Job Dependency Management**:
- Critical job execution order (e.g., CLOSEFIL before batch updates, OPENFIL after)
- No automated workflow orchestration in Version 1
- Manual JCL submission with job interdependencies
- Risk of data corruption if job sequence violated

**Job Monitoring and Recovery**:
- Manual job status monitoring via SDSF or equivalent
- Abends require manual diagnosis and restart
- No automated restart/recovery procedures
- Checkpoint/restart not implemented for long-running jobs
- Mitigation: Implement job scheduler (e.g., CA Workload Automation, Control-M) with dependency management

#### 2.4.5.5 VSAM Dataset Reorganization

**Reorganization Requirements**:
- VSAM datasets with frequent inserts/deletes become fragmented
- Performance degradation over time
- Periodic REPRO (unload/reload) operations required
- Requires downtime for affected files

**Reorganization Schedule**:
- TRANSACT file: Monthly reorganization recommended (high insert volume)
- Master files: Quarterly reorganization (lower volatility)
- Reference files: Annual reorganization (static data)
- Backup before reorganization mandatory

# 3. Technology Stack

## 3.1 Overview and Architecture Context

### 3.1.1 Technology Foundation

CardDemo is built on a **traditional IBM z/OS mainframe technology stack**, representing the established architectural patterns and development practices of enterprise legacy systems. This is a deliberate design choice aligned with the application's purpose as a reference implementation for AWS Mainframe Modernization services, where authenticity to real-world mainframe environments is essential for effective tool validation and migration pathway demonstration.

The technology stack reflects the mainframe computing paradigm that has powered mission-critical enterprise applications for decades, incorporating character-based user interfaces (3270 terminals), transaction processing frameworks (CICS), hierarchical file systems (VSAM), and procedural programming languages (COBOL). Unlike modern cloud-native architectures that embrace microservices, containerization, and distributed computing patterns, CardDemo intentionally employs the monolithic, tightly-coupled architectural approach characteristic of legacy mainframe applications.

This technology stack serves three critical purposes within the AWS Mainframe Modernization ecosystem:

**Tool Validation and Testing**: The authentic mainframe technology stack enables AWS and partner organizations to validate discovery tools, test transformation engines, and verify migration utilities against genuine mainframe patterns rather than simplified simulations. Tools proven effective against CardDemo's technology stack have demonstrated readiness for real-world legacy system migrations.

**Migration Pathway Demonstration**: The application showcases two primary modernization strategies supported by AWS Mainframe Modernization services. The rehost approach uses Micro Focus Enterprise Server to execute the existing COBOL/CICS application on AWS infrastructure with minimal code changes, while the refactor approach leverages Blu Age automated refactoring to transform mainframe code into modern Java-based applications running on AWS cloud services.

**Educational Foundation**: The technology stack provides hands-on exposure to mainframe technologies for practitioners evaluating modernization opportunities, enabling developers familiar with modern architectures to understand the capabilities and constraints of legacy platforms they will be transforming.

### 3.1.2 Technology Evolution Roadmap

The current implementation (Version 1.0) represents a pure mainframe technology stack with no external integrations or cloud-native components. The planned Version 2.0 roadmap (Q1 2023 target) envisions selective integration with modern technologies while preserving the core mainframe foundation:

**Planned Database Integrations**: Integration with IBM Db2 relational database and IMS hierarchical database to demonstrate hybrid data persistence patterns where some data migrates to relational models while maintaining VSAM for specific use cases.

**Planned External Connectivity**: Addition of FTP/SFTP capabilities for file transfer operations, message queue (MQ) integration for asynchronous communication patterns, and distributed API exposure to enable integration with external systems and microservices architectures.

**AWS Cloud Services Integration**: Future incorporation of AWS services including S3 for storage modernization, RDS for relational database hosting, API Gateway for service exposure, Lambda for serverless functions, and CloudWatch for monitoring and observability.

These planned enhancements will demonstrate incremental modernization pathways where organizations selectively introduce modern technologies while preserving core mainframe business logic during transition periods.

## 3.2 Programming Languages

### 3.2.1 COBOL (Enterprise COBOL for z/OS)

**Selection Rationale**: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) serves as the exclusive application programming language for CardDemo, representing the dominant language for mainframe business applications since the 1960s. COBOL's selection is intentional and authentic to legacy enterprise systems, providing the verbose, self-documenting syntax and fixed-format structure characteristic of mainframe development practices.

**Version and Dialect**: The application uses Enterprise COBOL for z/OS, conforming to COBOL-85 standards or later. The specific compiler version is not constrained, as the code employs standard COBOL features compatible across contemporary mainframe COBOL compilers. This version flexibility demonstrates the portability of well-structured COBOL code across compiler generations.

**Usage Scope and Distribution**:

**Online Transaction Programs (18 CICS Programs)**:
- Authentication: `COSGN00C.cbl` - User signon and session initialization
- Navigation: `COMEN01C.cbl` (main menu), `COADM01C.cbl` (admin menu)
- Account Management: `COACTVWC.cbl` (view), `COACTUPC.cbl` (update)
- Card Management: `COCRDLIC.cbl` (list), `COCRDSLC.cbl` (view), `COCRDUPC.cbl` (update)
- Transaction Processing: `COTRN00C.cbl` (list), `COTRN01C.cbl` (view), `COTRN02C.cbl` (add)
- Financial Services: `COBIL00C.cbl` (bill payment)
- Reporting: `CORPT00C.cbl` (report submission)
- User Administration: `COUSR00C.cbl` (list), `COUSR01C.cbl` (add), `COUSR02C.cbl` (update), `COUSR03C.cbl` (delete)

**Batch Processing Programs (10 Programs)**:
- Account Operations: `CBACT01C.cbl` (refresh accounts), `CBACT02C.cbl` (account processing), `CBACT03C.cbl` (additional account operations), `CBACT04C.cbl` (interest calculation)
- Transaction Operations: `CBTRN01C.cbl` (transaction utilities), `CBTRN02C.cbl` (daily posting), `CBTRN03C.cbl` (transaction processing)
- Statement Generation: `CBSTM03A.CBL` (statement engine), `CBSTM03B.CBL` (I/O subroutine)
- Customer Operations: `CBCUS01C.cbl` (customer file management)

**Shared Utilities**:
- Date Conversion: `CSUTLDTC.cbl` - Date validation and transformation services using Language Environment CEEDAYS

**COBOL Language Features Utilized**:

**Data Division Capabilities**:
- `PICTURE` clauses for precise data definition: `PIC 9(11)` (11-digit numeric), `PIC X(16)` (16-character alphanumeric), `PIC S9(10)V99` (signed decimal with 2 decimal places)
- `COMPUTATIONAL-3` (COMP-3) for packed decimal storage of financial amounts, optimizing space while preserving precision
- `REDEFINES` clauses for data overlays, enabling multiple interpretations of the same storage area (extensively used in BMS map copybooks)
- `88-level` condition names for readable boolean logic: `88 CDEMO-USER-TYPE-ADMIN VALUE 'A'`
- Fixed-length record structures with precise byte alignment for VSAM file layouts

**Procedure Division Patterns**:
- Structured programming with numbered paragraph sections (e.g., `1000-MAIN-PROCESSING`, `2000-VALIDATE-INPUT`, `9999-ABEND-ROUTINE`)
- `COPY` statements for modular code inclusion from copybook libraries
- `PERFORM` statements for procedural flow control with `UNTIL` and `VARYING` clauses
- `EVALUATE` statements for multi-way branching (modern equivalent of nested IF-THEN-ELSE)
- `CALL` statements for invoking Language Environment services and subroutines

**CICS Integration**:
- `EXEC CICS` command blocks for transaction processing, file I/O, screen handling, and system services
- `RESP` and `RESP2` fields for comprehensive error handling of CICS operations
- Execute Interface Block (EIB) access for transaction context: `EIBCALEN` (communication area length), `EIBAID` (attention identifier for function keys)

**Coding Style Characteristics**: The application intentionally employs diverse COBOL coding styles across programs to exercise modernization tools' parsing and transformation capabilities. Variations include inconsistent paragraph numbering schemes (some programs use 0100-PARA style, others use 1000-PARA style), different error handling patterns (some programs use centralized error paragraphs, others use inline error checking), and varied data structure organization (some programs define extensive working storage, others use minimal local variables). This intentional heterogeneity mirrors real-world legacy codebases developed by multiple teams over extended periods.

### 3.2.2 JCL (Job Control Language)

**Selection Rationale**: JCL serves as the scripting and orchestration language for batch processing on z/OS systems. JCL provides declarative specification of job execution parameters, dataset allocation, program invocation, and conditional execution logic required for mainframe batch workloads.

**Usage Scope**: While JCL job streams are not included in the repository source code (as they are typically customized per installation), the README.md documentation extensively references JCL jobs required for system operation:

**Initialization Jobs**:
- `DUSRSECJ` - User security file initialization using IEBGENER utility
- Dataset definition jobs for ACCTFILE, CARDFILE, CUSTFILE, XREFFILE, TRANSACT using IDCAMS

**Operational Jobs**:
- `CLOSEFIL` - File closure coordination using IEFBR14 before batch window
- `OPENFIL` - File opening coordination using IEFBR14 after batch completion
- `POSTTRAN` - Daily transaction posting job invoking CBTRN02C
- `INTCALC` - Interest calculation job invoking CBACT04C
- `COMBTRAN` - Transaction file combination using SORT utility
- `CREASTMT` - Statement generation job invoking CBSTM03A/B
- `TRANIDX` - Alternate index creation for transaction file access
- `DEFGDGB` - Generation Data Group base definition for statement archival

**JCL Features Required**:
- DD (Data Definition) statements for VSAM file allocation and sequential file processing
- EXEC statements for program invocation with PARM parameter passing
- COND parameters for conditional execution based on previous step return codes
- JCL procedures for reusable job step definitions
- Symbolic parameters for site-specific dataset naming (High-Level Qualifier substitution)
- GDG management for statement file versioning

**Integration Requirements**: JCL jobs coordinate with CICS regions through VSAM file sharing and transient data queue (TDQ) processing. The CORPT00C online program submits report requests to transient data queues, which trigger JCL job initiation for batch report generation, demonstrating the classic mainframe pattern of online-to-batch integration.

## 3.3 Frameworks and Runtime Environments

### 3.3.1 CICS Transaction Server

**Framework Overview**: CICS (Customer Information Control System) is IBM's premier transaction processing monitor for z/OS mainframe systems. CICS provides the complete runtime environment for online transaction processing, managing terminal I/O, program loading, task scheduling, file access, and transaction integrity for high-volume, mission-critical applications.

**Version**: The application uses standard CICS features compatible with contemporary CICS Transaction Server versions (CICS TS 5.x or later). No version-specific features are employed, ensuring portability across CICS releases.

**Architecture and Capabilities**:

CICS operates as a long-running region (address space) on z/OS that multiplexes thousands of concurrent terminal sessions across shared program instances. The CICS kernel provides comprehensive transaction management including:

**Transaction Control**: CICS manages the complete transaction lifecycle from user attention identifier (AID) receipt through program invocation, resource allocation, execution, and transaction commit or rollback. Each user interaction constitutes a discrete transaction with defined start and end points.

**Task Management**: CICS implements cooperative multitasking where programs voluntarily release control to CICS at logical points (typically at SEND MAP or RETURN commands). This pseudo-conversational model releases resources between user interactions, enabling efficient resource utilization for thousands of concurrent users.

**Terminal Management**: CICS handles 3270 terminal protocol communication, managing terminal attention identifiers (Enter, PF1-PF24, PA1-PA2, Clear keys), screen buffer transmission, and terminal attributes (color, highlighting, field protection). Programs interact with terminals through BMS (Basic Mapping Support) rather than direct terminal I/O.

**Program Management**: CICS loads programs into memory on first use and maintains them in storage pools for subsequent transaction invocations. The NEWCOPY command forces program reloads after compilation, supporting dynamic application updates without region recycling.

**File Control**: CICS provides high-level file access services abstracted from physical access methods. Programs issue CICS file control commands (READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, STARTBR, READNEXT, READPREV, ENDBR) which CICS translates into appropriate VSAM operations with automatic record locking and buffer management.

**Transaction Integrity**: CICS ensures ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) for transaction processing through automatic commit and rollback processing. File updates are automatically backed out if transaction failures occur.

**CICS Commands Used in CardDemo**:

**Terminal I/O Commands**:
- `EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP` - Receive user input from terminal screen with automatic field unprotection and data translation from display format to program format
- `EXEC CICS SEND MAP` - Send screen output to terminal with field protection, attribute application (color, intensity, highlighting), and cursor positioning
- `EXEC CICS SEND TEXT` - Send unformatted text messages for error conditions or confirmation messages

**File Access Commands**:
- `EXEC CICS READ` - Random read by primary key with optional UPDATE lock for subsequent REWRITE
- `EXEC CICS WRITE` - Add new record with duplicate key detection
- `EXEC CICS REWRITE` - Update existing record previously read with UPDATE lock
- `EXEC CICS DELETE` - Remove record by key
- `EXEC CICS STARTBR` - Initiate browse operation with full or partial key positioning
- `EXEC CICS READNEXT` - Sequential forward read during browse
- `EXEC CICS READPREV` - Sequential backward read during browse
- `EXEC CICS ENDBR` - Terminate browse operation and release browse resources

**Program Control Commands**:
- `EXEC CICS RETURN` - Terminate transaction and return control to CICS with optional COMMAREA and TRANSID for pseudo-conversational chaining
- `EXEC CICS XCTL` - Transfer control to another program within same transaction without returning
- `EXEC CICS LINK` - Call another program as subroutine with return to caller

**System Services Commands**:
- `EXEC CICS ASKTIME` - Retrieve current system time as ABSTIME value
- `EXEC CICS FORMATTIME` - Convert ABSTIME to formatted date/time string
- `EXEC CICS ABEND` - Abnormal end with transaction rollback and dump generation
- `EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION` - Declare exception handlers for CICS conditions (now superseded by RESP code checking)

**CICS Resource Definitions**:

The application requires comprehensive CICS System Definition (CSD) resource definitions organized into a `CARDDEMO` group:

**Transaction Definitions (20+ Transactions)**:
- `CC00` - Signon transaction invoking COSGN00C
- `CM00` - Main menu transaction invoking COMEN01C
- `CA00` - Admin menu transaction invoking COADM01C
- `CAVW` - Account view transaction invoking COACTVWC
- `CAUP` - Account update transaction invoking COACTUPC
- `CCLI`, `CCVW`, `CCUP` - Card list, view, update transactions
- `CT00`, `CT01`, `CT02` - Transaction list, view, add transactions
- `CBIL` - Bill payment transaction
- `CRPT` - Report submission transaction
- `CU00`, `CU01`, `CU02`, `CU03` - User list, add, update, delete transactions

**Program Definitions (28+ Programs)**:
All COBOL programs require CICS program resource definitions specifying program name, language (COBOL), DATALOCATION(ANY), and EXECKEY(USER) attributes.

**File Definitions (13+ Files)**:
VSAM file resource definitions including: USRSEC, ACCTFILE, CARDFILE, CUSTFILE, XREFFILE, TRANSACT, DALYTRAN, DALYREJS, TCATBAL, DISCGRP, TRANCATG, TRANTYPE. Each file definition specifies DSNAME (dataset name), LSRPOOL settings for buffer management, and file status attributes (ENABLED, OPENED).

**Mapset Definitions (17 Mapsets)**:
BMS mapset resource definitions for all screen layouts (COSGN00, COMEN01, COADM01, COACTVW, COACTUP, COCRDLI, COCRDSL, COCRDUP, COTRN00, COTRN01, COTRN02, COBIL00, CORPT00, COUSR00-03).

**Resource Group Management**: All resources are organized into the `CARDDEMO` group for simplified installation and management. The group can be installed with a single CEDA INSTALL GROUP(CARDDEMO) command, enabling or disabling the entire application atomically.

**CICS Integration Pattern**: CardDemo implements the classic CICS pseudo-conversational pattern where each program invocation follows this flow:

1. CICS receives attention identifier (Enter, PF key) from terminal
2. CICS initiates transaction specified in TRANSID
3. Transaction invokes associated program
4. Program receives COMMAREA from previous transaction (if chained)
5. Program issues RECEIVE MAP to retrieve terminal input
6. Program performs business logic and file access
7. Program issues SEND MAP to display results
8. Program issues RETURN with COMMAREA and TRANSID for next interaction
9. CICS terminates transaction and releases all resources
10. User views screen and enters next request, repeating the cycle

This pattern ensures that CICS resources (program storage, file buffers, terminal control blocks) are held only during active program execution, not during user think time, enabling efficient resource sharing across thousands of concurrent users.

### 3.3.2 BMS (Basic Mapping Support)

**Framework Overview**: BMS is CICS's presentation framework for managing 3270 terminal screen layouts and field-level I/O. BMS provides a declarative mapping language for defining screen formats, field attributes, and data mapping between terminal display format and program data structures.

**Architecture**: BMS operates as a two-stage translation and runtime framework:

**Compile-Time Map Generation**: BMS source files (`.bms` files) undergo BMS macro processing to generate two outputs:
- **Physical Map**: Binary load module containing terminal control sequences, field positions, and attribute bytes for actual screen rendering
- **Symbolic Map**: COBOL copybook defining data structures (map control fields, input/output areas) that programs use to exchange data with BMS

**Runtime Map Processing**: During program execution, CICS BMS runtime services:
- Accept high-level SEND MAP commands from programs
- Merge program data with physical map definitions
- Apply terminal attributes (protection, numeric, skip, fill, modified data tag)
- Transmit formatted 3270 data streams to terminals
- Receive modified data from terminals via RECEIVE MAP commands
- Extract field values and set input flags (length fields, attribute flags)
- Populate program data structures with user input

**BMS Map Definitions (17 Screen Layouts)**:

Each BMS map source file defines a complete screen layout:

- `COSGN00.bms` - User signon screen with user ID, password fields (password field is non-display)
- `COMEN01.bms` - Main menu with 10 selectable options and option selection field
- `COADM01.bms` - Admin menu with 4 administrative function options
- `COACTVW.bms` - Account view screen displaying account ID, balances, limits, dates (view-only protected fields)
- `COACTUP.bms` - Account update screen with modifiable fields (credit limit, expiration date, status)
- `COCRDLI.bms` - Card list screen displaying up to 7 cards per page with selection field per card
- `COCRDSL.bms` - Card detail view with comprehensive card information
- `COCRDUP.bms` - Card update screen for modifying card attributes
- `COTRN00.bms` - Transaction list with filtering options and multi-line display (7 transactions per screen)
- `COTRN01.bms` - Transaction detail view with merchant, amount, category information
- `COTRN02.bms` - Transaction add screen for new transaction entry
- `COBIL00.bms` - Bill payment screen showing current balance and payment amount field
- `CORPT00.bms` - Report request screen with date range selection and report type options
- `COUSR00.bms` - User list screen displaying user records with pagination
- `COUSR01.bms` - User add screen for new user creation
- `COUSR02.bms` - User update screen for credential and role modification
- `COUSR03.bms` - User delete confirmation screen

**BMS Macro Language Features**:

**DFHMSD (Map Set Definition)**: Defines the container for one or more maps with common characteristics:
```
DFHMSD TYPE=&SYSPARM,LANG=COBOL,MODE=INOUT,TIOAPFX=YES,
       STORAGE=AUTO,EXTATT=YES,CTRL=(ALARM,FREEKB)
```
- `TYPE=MAP` generates physical map, `TYPE=DSECT` generates symbolic map (COBOL copybook)
- `LANG=COBOL` specifies COBOL data structure generation
- `MODE=INOUT` indicates bidirectional data flow (input and output)
- `TIOAPFX=YES` includes terminal I/O area prefix fields
- `STORAGE=AUTO` enables automatic storage acquisition
- `EXTATT=YES` enables extended 3270 attributes (color, highlighting)
- `CTRL=(ALARM,FREEKB)` sounds alarm and unlocks keyboard on send

**DFHMDI (Map Definition)**: Defines individual screen layout within mapset:
```
DFHMDI SIZE=(24,80),LINE=1,COLUMN=1
```
- `SIZE=(24,80)` specifies standard 3270 screen dimensions (24 rows, 80 columns)
- `LINE=1,COLUMN=1` positions map at top-left screen origin

**DFHMDF (Map Field Definition)**: Defines individual screen fields with position, length, and attributes:
```
DFHMDF POS=(05,01),LENGTH=11,ATTRB=(ASKIP,NORM,PROT),
       INITIAL='Account ID:',COLOR=BLUE
DFHMDF POS=(05,13),LENGTH=11,ATTRB=(UNPROT,NUM,FSET,IC),
       COLOR=TURQUOISE,HILIGHT=UNDERLINE
```

**Field Attributes**:
- **Protection**: `PROT` (protected, display only), `UNPROT` (unprotected, user modifiable), `ASKIP` (autoskip, protects and moves cursor to next field)
- **Display Intensity**: `NORM` (normal intensity), `BRT` (bright/high intensity), `DRK` (non-display for password fields)
- **Data Type**: `NUM` (numeric only), `ALPHA` (alphabetic only), no attribute (alphanumeric)
- **Control**: `IC` (initial cursor, positions cursor at this field on first display), `FSET` (field set, forces modified data tag even if unchanged)
- **Extended Attributes**:
  - `COLOR`: BLUE (headers), YELLOW (prompts/labels), TURQUOISE (data entry fields), GREEN (success messages), RED (error messages), NEUTRAL (general text)
  - `HILIGHT`: UNDERLINE (input fields), BLINK (critical alerts), REVERSE (attention items)
  - `PICIN/PICOUT`: Edit patterns for formatted numeric input/output
  - `JUSTIFY`: LEFT, RIGHT for field justification
  - `ZERO`: Zero-fill numeric fields

**BMS Copybook Generation**: When BMS maps are processed with `TYPE=DSECT`, BMS generates COBOL copybooks in the `app/cpy-bms/` directory. Each map produces two data structure layouts:

**Input Structure (AI suffix)**: Physical layout mirroring actual 3270 data stream format:
```cobol
01 MAPNAMEI.
   02 FILLER PIC X(12).               *> Reserved prefix
   02 FLDNAMEL COMP PIC S9(4).        *> Field length (binary)
   02 FLDNAMEF PIC X.                 *> Field flags
   02 FILLER REDEFINES FLDNAMEF.
      03 FLDNAMEA PIC X.              *> Attribute byte
   02 FLDNAMEI PIC X(nn).             *> Field input data
```

**Output Structure (AO suffix)**: REDEFINES overlay providing named attribute flag access:
```cobol
01 MAPNAMEO REDEFINES MAPNAMEI.
   02 FILLER PIC X(12).
   02 FLDNAMEL COMP PIC S9(4).
   02 FLDNAMEC PIC X.                 *> Color attribute
   02 FLDNAMEP PIC X.                 *> Protection attribute
   02 FLDNAMEH PIC X.                 *> Highlighting attribute
   02 FLDNAMEV PIC X.                 *> Validation attribute
   02 FLDNAMEO PIC X(nn).             *> Field output data
```

Programs reference these structures to receive user input (`EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP(...) INTO(MAPNAMEI)`) and send screen output (`EXEC CICS SEND MAP(...) FROM(MAPNAMEO)`), with CICS BMS runtime handling all terminal control sequence generation and data stream parsing.

**Screen Layout Conventions**: All CardDemo screens follow consistent layout patterns:

- **Row 1**: Application title "AWS Mainframe Modernization - CardDemo" in BLUE
- **Row 2**: Screen-specific title (e.g., "Signon", "Main Menu", "Account View") in YELLOW
- **Row 3**: Date/time display and user identification in NEUTRAL
- **Rows 4-22**: Functional screen content (data fields, lists, menus)
- **Row 23**: Function key help text (e.g., "PF3=Return PF7=Up PF8=Down") in TURQUOISE
- **Row 24**: Message line for errors, confirmations, instructions in GREEN (success) or RED (errors)

This consistent layout provides predictable user experience across all application screens, typical of well-designed mainframe applications.

### 3.3.3 IBM Language Environment (LE)

**Framework Overview**: IBM Language Environment provides common runtime services for high-level language programs on z/OS, including COBOL, C, C++, PL/I, and FORTRAN. Language Environment abstracts platform-specific services and provides portable APIs for date/time handling, mathematical functions, condition handling, storage management, and inter-language communication.

**Version**: The application uses standard Language Environment callable services compatible with Language Environment for z/OS Version 2 or later.

**Services Utilized**:

**Date and Time Services**: The date conversion utility (`CSUTLDTC.cbl`) invokes Language Environment date services:

- `CEEDAYS` - Convert calendar date to Lilian format (days since October 15, 1582, start of Gregorian calendar)
- `CEEDATE` - Convert Lilian format to calendar date
- `CEESECS` - Convert date and time to seconds since January 1, 1970 (Unix epoch)

These services provide robust date arithmetic, leap year handling, and calendar conversion capabilities superior to COBOL intrinsic date functions. The utility uses VSTRING (varying-length string) descriptors to pass parameters to Language Environment services.

**Condition Handling**: Programs use Language Environment condition handling for controlled abnormal termination:

- `CEE3ABD` - Controlled abend with user abend code and optional dump generation
- Provides cleaner abend processing than COBOL STOP RUN or GOBACK for diagnostic purposes

**Runtime Options**: CICS programs execute under Language Environment runtime with options controlling:
- Storage allocation strategies (heap, stack management)
- Condition handling behavior (trap/no trap for specific conditions)
- Runtime debugging and trace options
- Inter-language communication enablement

Language Environment runtime options are typically specified through CICS program definitions or region-level defaults rather than program-specific settings.

**Integration Pattern**: Programs invoke Language Environment services through COBOL `CALL` statements with specific parameter passing conventions. The date utility (`CSUTLDTC.cbl`) encapsulates Language Environment calls, providing higher-level date validation services to calling programs without requiring each program to manage VSTRING descriptors and parameter complexity directly.

## 3.4 Data Management and Storage

### 3.4.1 VSAM (Virtual Storage Access Method)

**Technology Overview**: VSAM is IBM's high-performance file system for z/OS mainframe storage management. VSAM provides indexed, sequential, and relative record organization with built-in buffering, caching, and access method optimization. Unlike relational databases, VSAM is a file-based storage system where each file is a self-contained dataset with defined record structure, index organization, and access characteristics.

**Version**: Standard z/OS VSAM (DFSMS/MVS version-independent, as VSAM is integral to z/OS operating system). The application uses VSAM features available in all contemporary z/OS releases.

**Selection Rationale**: VSAM was selected as the exclusive data persistence layer to authentically represent traditional mainframe data management patterns. VSAM remains the predominant storage technology for mainframe applications due to its performance characteristics, tight integration with z/OS security, and comprehensive support for high-volume transaction processing. For CardDemo's modernization demonstration purposes, VSAM provides the authentic legacy storage layer that tools must transform when migrating to cloud-native architectures.

**VSAM Dataset Organization Types**:

**Key-Sequenced Data Sets (KSDS)**: Primary dataset type for CardDemo's master files, providing indexed access with automatic record ordering by primary key:

- `USRSEC` (User Security File)
  - **Record Length**: 80 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: User ID (8 characters, position 0-7)
  - **Purpose**: Authentication credentials, role assignments
  - **Copybook**: `CSUSR01Y.cpy` (SEC-USER-DATA)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by user ID for login validation

- `ACCTFILE` (Account Master File)
  - **Record Length**: 300 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Account ID (11 digits, position 0-10)
  - **Purpose**: Account balances, credit limits, lifecycle dates
  - **Copybook**: `CVACT01Y.cpy` (ACCOUNT-RECORD)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by account ID for inquiries, update-in-place for balance modifications
  - **Key Fields**: Account current balance (S9(10)V99 COMP-3), credit limit (S9(10)V99 COMP-3), expiration date (10-char ISO-8601)

- `CARDFILE` (Card Master File)
  - **Record Length**: 150 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Card number (16 characters, position 0-15)
  - **Purpose**: Credit card details, CVV codes, expiration dates
  - **Copybook**: `CVACT02Y.cpy` (CARD-RECORD)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by card number, browse by partial account ID key for card listing
  - **Key Fields**: Card CVV code (3 digits), expiration date (7-char MM/YYYY), embossed name (50 characters)

- `CUSTFILE` (Customer Master File)
  - **Record Length**: 500 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Customer ID (9 digits, position 0-8)
  - **Purpose**: Customer demographic, contact, identification information
  - **Copybook**: `CVCUS01Y.cpy` / `CUSTREC.cpy` (CUSTOMER-RECORD)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by customer ID
  - **Key Fields**: Name (50 characters), address fields (50+25+25 characters), phone (10 characters), government ID (9 characters)

- `XREFFILE` (Cross-Reference File)
  - **Record Length**: 50 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Composite key (Customer ID + Account ID + Card Number, position 0-35)
  - **Purpose**: Referential integrity enforcement linking customers to accounts to cards
  - **Copybook**: `CVACT03Y.cpy` (XREF-RECORD)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by full composite key or partial key for relationship validation

- `TRANSACT` (Transaction Master File)
  - **Record Length**: 350 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Transaction ID (16 characters, position 0-15)
  - **Purpose**: All credit and debit transaction records
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA05Y.cpy` (TRAN-RECORD)
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by transaction ID, browse by card number for transaction history
  - **Key Fields**: Transaction amount (S9(09)V99 COMP-3), merchant name/city/zip (50+25+10 characters), transaction type/category codes (2+4 characters), origination/processing timestamps (26 characters ISO-8601 with microseconds)

- `TCATBAL` (Transaction Category Balance File)
  - **Record Length**: 50 bytes
  - **Key Structure**: Account ID + Transaction Category (11+4 characters)
  - **Purpose**: Aggregated balances by transaction category for financial reporting
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA01Y.cpy`
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by account + category for balance inquiries and updates

- `DISCGRP` (Disclosure Group File)
  - **Record Length**: 50 bytes
  - **Purpose**: Disclosure group reference data for regulatory compliance
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA02Y.cpy`
  - **Access Pattern**: Sequential scan for reference data loading

- `TRANCATG` (Transaction Category File)
  - **Record Length**: 60 bytes
  - **Purpose**: Transaction category definitions and interest rates
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA04Y.cpy`
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by category code, sequential for category listing

- `TRANTYPE` (Transaction Type File)
  - **Record Length**: 60 bytes
  - **Purpose**: Transaction type reference data (Purchase, Payment, Cash Advance, etc.)
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA03Y.cpy`
  - **Access Pattern**: Random by type code for transaction validation

**Sequential Datasets**: Used for batch processing input/output files:

- `DALYTRAN.PS` (Daily Transaction Feed)
  - **Record Length**: 350 bytes (identical to TRANSACT structure)
  - **Organization**: Physical Sequential (PS)
  - **Purpose**: Daily transaction input file for batch posting
  - **Copybook**: `CVTRA06Y.cpy` (DALYTRAN-RECORD)
  - **Processing**: Sequential read by CBTRN02C daily posting program

- `DALYTRAN.PS.INIT` (Transaction Database Initialization)
  - **Record Length**: 350 bytes
  - **Purpose**: Initial transaction data load for database setup
  - **Processing**: Loaded via IDCAMS REPRO into TRANSACT file

- `DALYREJS` (Daily Rejects File)
  - **Record Length**: 430 bytes (350-byte transaction + 80-byte reject reason)
  - **Organization**: Sequential
  - **Purpose**: Rejected transactions with diagnostic error codes
  - **Processing**: Written by CBTRN02C when transactions fail validation

**Generation Data Groups (GDG)**: Versioned sequential datasets for statement archival:

- **Purpose**: Historical statement retention with automatic generation management
- **Usage**: Statement generation job (`CREASTMT`) writes statements to GDG datasets, creating new generation with each execution
- **Setup**: `DEFGDGB` job defines GDG base with retention parameters (number of generations to retain)
- **Access**: Generational qualifiers (+1 for next, 0 for current, -1/-2 for previous) enable referencing specific statement versions

**VSAM Dataset Characteristics**:

**Control Interval (CI) and Control Area (CA)**: VSAM stores records in fixed-size control intervals (typical sizes: 4KB, 8KB, 16KB) grouped into control areas. CI size affects I/O efficiency (larger CIs reduce I/O operations but may waste space for small records). The catalog listing (`app/catlg/LISTCAT.txt`) documents CISIZE attributes for each dataset.

**Record Key Structure**: KSDS primary keys support:
- Full key access (direct record retrieval)
- Partial key positioning (STARTBR with partial key for range scans)
- Generic key searching (browse starting with key prefix)

**Alternate Indexes (AIX)**: The `TRANIDX` job creates alternate indexes on the TRANSACT file to support browsing transactions by card number (alternate key) rather than primary key (transaction ID). AIX enable efficient access patterns not supported by primary key alone.

**File Status Codes**: VSAM operations return two-byte status codes indicating operation results:
- `00` - Successful completion
- `10` - End of file (sequential read)
- `21` - Sequence error (invalid key order for sequential add)
- `22` - Duplicate key (attempted to write record with existing key)
- `23` - Record not found (READ/DELETE with non-existent key)
- `24` - Boundary violation (record length mismatch)
- `92` - Logic error (improper file state for operation)
- `93` - Resource not available (file not open or CICS file disabled)

Batch programs check file status after every I/O operation, performing error recovery or reject processing for non-zero status codes.

**VSAM Buffering and Caching**: CICS Local Shared Resources (LSR) pools provide shared buffering across all transactions accessing VSAM files. LSR pool configuration optimizes memory utilization and I/O performance through:
- Buffer pool sharing across concurrent transactions
- Look-aside caching for frequently accessed records
- Read-ahead buffering for sequential processing
- Deferred write buffering for update operations

LSR settings are specified in CICS file resource definitions, typically using system-wide default LSR pools.

**VSAM Security Integration**: VSAM datasets integrate with RACF (Resource Access Control Facility) for enterprise security management:
- Dataset protection through RACF profiles
- Access authorization checking (read, update, delete, control privileges)
- Audit trail generation for security-relevant file operations
- Password protection for VSAM clusters (alternative to RACF for smaller installations)

The `app/catlg/LISTCAT.txt` catalog listing shows RACF indicators and security attributes for defined datasets.

### 3.4.2 IDCAMS (Access Method Services)

**Utility Overview**: IDCAMS is the command-line utility for VSAM dataset definition, maintenance, and management operations. IDCAMS provides comprehensive dataset lifecycle management through declarative command syntax.

**Version**: Standard z/OS IDCAMS (component of DFSMS/MVS data management subsystem).

**IDCAMS Commands Used**:

**DEFINE CLUSTER**: Creates new VSAM Key-Sequenced Data Set with index component:
```
DEFINE CLUSTER (NAME(hlq.ACCTFILE) -
       RECORDSIZE(300 300) -
       KEYS(11 0) -
       VOLUMES(volser) -
       CYLINDERS(10 5) -
       SHAREOPTIONS(2 3))
```
- `RECORDSIZE(300 300)` specifies fixed 300-byte records (average max)
- `KEYS(11 0)` defines 11-byte key starting at offset 0
- `CYLINDERS(10 5)` allocates 10 primary cylinders, 5 secondary extents
- `SHAREOPTIONS(2 3)` enables file sharing between batch and CICS (option 2 for cross-region, option 3 for cross-system)

**REPRO**: Copies records between datasets, used for data loading:
```
REPRO INFILE(input-dd) OUTFILE(output-dd)
```
Loads ASCII test data files into VSAM datasets by copying from sequential input to KSDS output.

**DELETE**: Removes VSAM clusters and associated components:
```
DELETE hlq.ACCTFILE CLUSTER
```
Deletes both data and index components. Used in file refresh scenarios before redefining datasets.

**LISTCAT**: Lists catalog entries and dataset attributes:
```
LISTCAT ENTRIES(hlq.*) ALL
```
Produces comprehensive dataset documentation showing KEYLEN, CISIZE, AVGLRECL, BUFSPACE, volume allocations, record counts, and RACF attributes. The `app/catlg/LISTCAT.txt` file contains sample LISTCAT output documenting dataset configurations.

**ALTER**: Modifies dataset attributes without recreating dataset:
```
ALTER hlq.ACCTFILE FREESPACE(20 10)
```
Changes FREESPACE (percentage of free space in CIs/CAs for insert operations) or other modifiable attributes.

**IDCAMS Usage Pattern**: IDCAMS commands are typically embedded in JCL job streams with SYSIN DD * inline commands or SYSIN DD DSN= referencing command libraries. Installation procedures use IDCAMS to define all VSAM datasets during initial system setup.

### 3.4.3 Data Format and Character Encoding

**Character Set**: EBCDIC (Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code) is the native character encoding for z/OS systems. All COBOL programs, copybooks, BMS maps, and VSAM data files use EBCDIC encoding. Character values, collating sequences, and code page mappings differ significantly from ASCII/UTF-8 systems.

**ASCII Test Data**: The `app/data/ASCII/` directory contains ASCII-encoded test data files for portability to non-mainframe systems:

- `acctdata.txt` - 50 account records, fixed-width, positional format
- `carddata.txt` - 50 card records, fixed-width format
- `custdata.txt` - 50 customer records, fixed-width format
- `cardxref.txt` - Cross-reference records linking customers, accounts, cards
- `tcatbalf.txt` - Transaction category balance initial data
- `trancatg.txt` - 18 transaction category definitions with interest rates
- `trantype.txt` - 7 transaction type reference data
- `discgrp.txt` - Disclosure group reference data
- `usrsec.txt` - User security records (credentials for test users)

These ASCII files must be transferred to z/OS in binary mode (not text mode) and converted to EBCDIC during the load process to prevent character translation corruption.

**Numeric Data Formats**:

**DISPLAY Numeric (PIC 9)**: Character representation of digits, each digit occupies one byte in EBCDIC (F0-F9 hex). Used for display fields and external data interfaces.

**PACKED DECIMAL (COMP-3)**: Binary Coded Decimal format where each digit occupies 4 bits (nibble), with sign nibble in low-order position. A PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3 field (7 integer digits, 2 decimal places, signed) occupies 5 bytes. Used extensively for financial amounts to preserve decimal precision without floating-point rounding errors.

**BINARY (COMP)**: Standard two's complement binary integers. PIC S9(4) COMP occupies 2 bytes (halfword), PIC S9(9) COMP occupies 4 bytes (fullword). Used for counters, subscripts, and length fields (BMS copybooks use COMP for field length fields).

**Date and Time Formats**:

**Date Format**: ISO-8601 extended format `YYYY-MM-DD` (10 characters display). Example: `2022-07-15` represents July 15, 2022. All date fields in master files use this consistent format enabling direct string comparison for date range filtering.

**Timestamp Format**: ISO-8601 with microsecond precision `YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmmmmm` (26 characters). Example: `2022-07-15-14.30.45.123456` represents 2:30:45 PM and 123,456 microseconds. Used in TRANSACT file for origination and processing timestamps.

**Business Identifier Formats**:

- **Account ID**: 11-digit numeric, zero-padded (e.g., `00000123456`)
- **Customer ID**: 9-digit numeric (e.g., `000123456`)
- **Card Number**: 16-character alphanumeric (follows credit card number format patterns)
- **Transaction ID**: 16-character unique identifier (system-generated)
- **User ID**: 8-character alphanumeric (e.g., `ADMIN001`)

**Record Layout Documentation**: All record structures are precisely documented in COBOL copybooks with PICTURE clauses specifying exact byte positions, lengths, and data types. This explicit data contract approach differs from relational databases where schema metadata is managed by the DBMS rather than application code.

## 3.5 System Software and Utilities

### 3.5.1 z/OS Operating System

**Platform**: IBM z/OS is the enterprise-class operating system for IBM mainframe systems (z14, z15, z16 processor families). z/OS provides the foundational platform services including task management, storage management, I/O subsystems, security services, and job scheduling.

**Version**: The application is compatible with z/OS Version 2.4 or later. No version-specific features are exploited, ensuring broad z/OS platform compatibility.

**z/OS Services Utilized**:

**MVS Job Entry Subsystem (JES2/JES3)**: Manages batch job submission, scheduling, and output handling. JCL job streams are submitted to JES, which schedules job execution, allocates datasets, initiates programs, and manages spool files (SYSOUT).

**Catalog Services**: Maintains system catalog (`CATALOG.XXXXXXXX.YYYY`) that stores dataset metadata, volume allocations, and dataset characteristics. All VSAM datasets are cataloged, enabling symbolic dataset references in JCL and CICS file definitions without hard-coded volume serial numbers.

**DFSMS (Data Facility Storage Management Subsystem)**: Provides storage management services including automatic dataset placement (storage class assignment), space management, backup services, and migration/recall for HSM (Hierarchical Storage Manager). The `app/catlg/LISTCAT.txt` shows SMSDATA attributes including STORAGECLASS and LBACKUP timestamps.

**RACF (Resource Access Control Facility)**: Enterprise security manager providing authentication, authorization, and audit services. Controls access to datasets, programs, transactions, and system resources through security profiles and access control lists. While RACF is referenced in documentation, CardDemo implements application-level security (USRSEC file) rather than full RACF integration for portability to non-RACF environments.

**WLM (Workload Manager)**: Manages system resources and prioritizes work based on business objectives. Assigns service classes to CICS regions and batch jobs to ensure performance goals are met.

### 3.5.2 z/OS Utility Programs

**IEBGENER**: General-purpose dataset copy utility. The `DUSRSECJ` job uses IEBGENER to load user security file from sequential input:
```
//SYSIN DD *
  GENERATE MAXFLDS=1
  RECORD FIELD=(80,1,,1)
/*
```
Copies 80-byte records from SYSIN to VSAM output, supporting initial data loading.

**IEFBR14**: Null program ("dummy" program that immediately returns) used for dataset allocation and deallocation operations. The `CLOSEFIL` and `OPENFIL` jobs use IEFBR14 with DD statements to close files before batch processing and reopen files after batch completion:
```
//STEP1   EXEC PGM=IEFBR14
//ACCTFILE DD DSN=hlq.ACCTFILE,DISP=OLD
```
The `DISP=OLD` allocation disposition forces file access serialization, ensuring exclusive control during batch windows.

**SORT**: High-performance sorting and merging utility. The `COMBTRAN` job uses SORT to merge system transaction file with daily transaction feed:
```
//SORTIN01 DD DSN=hlq.TRANSACT,DISP=SHR
//SORTIN02 DD DSN=hlq.DALYTRAN,DISP=SHR
//SORTOUT  DD DSN=hlq.TRANSACT.COMBINED,DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
//SYSIN DD *
  SORT FIELDS=(1,16,CH,A)
  MERGE FIELDS=(1,16,CH,A)
/*
```
Sorts/merges based on transaction ID key field (16 characters starting at byte 1), combining multiple input files into single sorted output.

### 3.5.3 CICS Utilities

**DFHCSDUP (CICS System Definition Utility)**: Batch utility for manipulating CICS System Definition (CSD) file. Used to add, modify, delete, and copy resource definitions:
```
//SYSIN DD *
INITIALIZE
DEFINE GROUP(CARDDEMO) DESCRIPTION('CardDemo Application')
DEFINE TRANSACTION(CC00) GROUP(CARDDEMO) PROGRAM(COSGN00C)
DEFINE PROGRAM(COSGN00C) GROUP(CARDDEMO) LANGUAGE(COBOL)
DEFINE FILE(ACCTFILE) GROUP(CARDDEMO) DSNAME(hlq.ACCTFILE)
DEFINE MAPSET(COSGN00) GROUP(CARDDEMO)
/*
```
Batch definition of all CardDemo resources for repeatable installation.

**CEDA (CICS Executive Definition and Administration)**: Online transaction for interactive resource definition. Provides browse, define, alter, delete, install, and discard functions:
```
CEDA DEFINE TRANSACTION(CC00) GROUP(CARDDEMO)
CEDA INSTALL GROUP(CARDDEMO)
```
Used by system administrators for runtime resource management.

**CEMT (CICS Master Terminal Transaction)**: Online transaction for runtime resource control and inquiry:
```
CEMT SET PROGRAM(COSGN00C) NEWCOPY
CEMT INQUIRE FILE(ACCTFILE)
CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) OPEN ENABLED
```
Essential for program refresh after compilation (NEWCOPY), file status checking, and file open/close operations.

**CECI (CICS Execute Command Interpreter)**: Online testing transaction allowing interactive execution of CICS commands:
```
CECI READ FILE(ACCTFILE) RIDFLD('00000123456')
```
Used by developers for testing file access, screen maps, and CICS commands without writing test programs.

## 3.6 Development Tools and Build Process

### 3.6.1 Source Code Management

**Git / GitHub**: The CardDemo repository is hosted on GitHub under Apache License 2.0, providing:
- Version control for all source artifacts (COBOL, copybooks, BMS maps)
- Collaborative development through pull requests and issue tracking
- Community contribution management per `CONTRIBUTING.md` guidelines
- Code of Conduct enforcement per Amazon Open Source Code of Conduct (`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`)

**Repository Structure**:
```
CardDemo/
├── app/
│   ├── cbl/         (28 COBOL programs)
│   ├── cpy/         (28 COBOL copybooks)
│   ├── bms/         (17 BMS map sources)
│   ├── cpy-bms/     (17 BMS generated copybooks)
│   ├── catlg/       (VSAM catalog snapshot)
│   └── data/ASCII/  (9 test data files)
├── README.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
└── LICENSE
```

### 3.6.2 Compilation and Build Process

**z/OS COBOL Compiler**: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS compiles COBOL source programs:

**Compilation Steps for CICS Programs**:
1. **CICS Translation**: CICS translator preprocesses EXEC CICS commands, generating COBOL CALL statements to CICS stubs
2. **COBOL Compilation**: Translated COBOL source is compiled with COPY statement resolution from copybook libraries
3. **Linkage Editing**: Object modules are link-edited with CICS interface modules to create executable load modules

**Compiler Options**: Typical compilation parameters include:
- `LIB` - Copybook library concatenation
- `CICS` - CICS translator activation
- `NODYNAM` - Static call resolution
- `RENT` - Reentrant code generation for CICS sharing
- `TRUNC(OPT)` - Optimized truncation
- `NUMPROC(PFD)` - Preferred sign processing for COMP-3 fields

**BMS Map Assembly**: BMS macro processor generates physical and symbolic maps:

1. **Physical Map Generation**: 
```
//STEP1 EXEC PGM=ASMA90,PARM='SYSPARM(MAP)'
//SYSIN DD DSN=hlq.BMS(COSGN00),DISP=SHR
```
Assembles `TYPE=MAP` to create load module for CICS mapset library.

2. **Symbolic Map Generation**:
```
//STEP2 EXEC PGM=ASMA90,PARM='SYSPARM(DSECT)'
//SYSIN DD DSN=hlq.BMS(COSGN00),DISP=SHR
```
Assembles `TYPE=DSECT` to create COBOL copybook for `app/cpy-bms/` directory.

**Build Sequence**: Complete application build requires:
1. BMS map assembly (both physical and symbolic maps)
2. COBOL program translation and compilation
3. Linkage editor execution to create load modules
4. CICS NEWCOPY commands for load module refresh

**Build Automation**: The README.md references "compile process followed by your mainframe shopfloor" indicating that CardDemo assumes existing mainframe build procedures rather than providing packaged build scripts. This approach aligns with mainframe development practices where each installation has established compilation procedures adapted to local standards and naming conventions.

### 3.6.3 Deployment and Installation

**High-Level Qualifier (HLQ)**: Mainframe dataset naming convention uses dot-separated qualifiers. Recommended HLQ is `AWS.M2`:

**Dataset Organization**:
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL` - JCL job streams (FB 80)
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC` - JCL procedures (FB 80)
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL` - COBOL source programs (FB 80)
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY` - COBOL copybooks (FB 80)
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.BMS` - BMS map sources (FB 80)
- `AWS.M2.LOADLIB` - Compiled load modules

All source datasets use Fixed-Block (FB) record format with 80-byte logical record length, standard for mainframe source code.

**Installation Steps** (per README.md):

1. **Source Upload**: Transfer source files from GitHub repository to z/OS partitioned datasets with BINARY transfer mode (critical for EBCDIC conversion)
2. **Dataset Definition**: Execute IDCAMS jobs to define VSAM clusters for all master and transaction files
3. **Data Loading**: Run initialization jobs (DUSRSECJ, account/card/customer load jobs) to populate master files with test data from `app/data/ASCII/` directory
4. **CICS Resource Definition**: Use DFHCSDUP or CEDA to define CARDDEMO resource group with all transactions, programs, files, and mapsets
5. **Resource Installation**: Execute `CEDA INSTALL GROUP(CARDDEMO)` to activate resources in CICS region
6. **Verification**: Test signon transaction (CC00) to validate successful installation

**Configuration Parameters**:
- HLQ customization for dataset naming
- VOLSER specification for DASD volume placement
- CICS region name and applid
- CICS CSD library allocation
- Load library concatenation in CICS DFHRPL

### 3.6.4 Testing and Validation

**Unit Testing**: Not explicitly implemented in the repository. Traditional mainframe unit testing approaches include:
- Manual testing through CICS transactions with test data
- CECI transaction for interactive command testing
- Batch program testing through JCL submission with test input files

**Integration Testing**: Validation of end-to-end workflows:
- User authentication through CC00 transaction
- Account management workflows (view, update)
- Card management workflows (list, view, update)
- Transaction entry and batch posting cycle
- Bill payment processing
- Report generation and statement creation

**Test Data**: The `app/data/ASCII/` directory provides comprehensive test data:
- 50 account records with varied balances and statuses
- 50 card records with corresponding customer and account associations
- 50 customer records with diverse demographic profiles
- Transaction category and type reference data
- User security records for multiple test users (admin and regular users)

**Validation Criteria**: Successful installation is validated through:
- Clean CICS region startup with CARDDEMO group installed
- Successful signon with test credentials
- Ability to navigate menus and access all functions
- Batch job successful completion without abends
- VSAM file status verification through LISTCAT commands

## 3.7 AWS Mainframe Modernization Integration

### 3.7.1 Target Migration Platform

**AWS Mainframe Modernization Service**: CardDemo is specifically designed for the AWS Mainframe Modernization service ecosystem, which provides managed runtime environments and transformation tools for legacy mainframe applications.

**Migration Strategy Options**:

**Rehost Approach - Micro Focus Enterprise Server**:
- **Runtime Environment**: Micro Focus Enterprise Server provides z/OS-compatible runtime on x86 Linux infrastructure
- **COBOL Compatibility**: Enterprise COBOL programs execute with minimal modification on Micro Focus COBOL runtime
- **CICS Emulation**: Enterprise Server Transaction Manager provides CICS API compatibility
- **VSAM Support**: Enterprise Server File Handler provides VSAM file access semantics on Unix/Linux filesystems
- **Migration Process**: Lift-and-shift mainframe applications to AWS cloud infrastructure with minimal code changes, preserving COBOL source code and business logic
- **Benefits**: Fastest migration path, lowest risk, preserves existing skills and operational procedures

**Refactor Approach - Blu Age Transformation**:
- **Automated Refactoring**: Blu Age analyzer and transformer parse COBOL/CICS/BMS source code and generate modern Java applications
- **Target Architecture**: Generated Spring Boot applications with JPA persistence and web-based UI
- **Transformation Scope**: COBOL business logic transformed to Java classes, VSAM files mapped to relational database tables, BMS maps converted to HTML/JavaScript web interfaces
- **Migration Process**: Automated code analysis, transformation rule application, generated code validation, manual refinement of transformation rules
- **Benefits**: Modernized architecture, cloud-native patterns, easier maintenance with contemporary skills

**Hybrid Modernization**: Incremental approach combining rehost and refactor where:
- Core business logic initially rehosted with Micro Focus
- Selected components progressively refactored to Java/Spring Boot
- Integration services bridge rehosted and refactored components
- Eventual complete transition to cloud-native architecture

### 3.7.2 Planned AWS Service Integrations

**Storage Modernization (Version 2.0 Roadmap)**:

**Amazon S3**: Object storage for unstructured data and archival:
- Migration target for sequential batch files (DALYTRAN, DALYREJS)
- Statement archival replacing Generation Data Groups
- Backup and disaster recovery storage
- Integration approach: VSAM-to-S3 gateway or refactored code with AWS SDK

**Amazon RDS**: Managed relational database services:
- Migration target for VSAM KSDS files (ACCTFILE, CARDFILE, CUSTFILE)
- Support for IBM Db2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle engines
- Schema design maps VSAM record layouts to relational tables
- Integration approach: Data replication tools or Blu Age-generated JPA entities

**Database Integrations**:

**IBM Db2 on z/OS**: Relational database integration (planned):
- Hybrid persistence with VSAM for transactional data, Db2 for analytical queries
- Demonstrates coexistence patterns during incremental modernization
- COBOL Db2 programs using EXEC SQL embedded SQL statements

**IBM IMS**: Hierarchical database integration (planned):
- IMS DL/I calls for hierarchical data access
- Common in mainframe customer/order hierarchies
- Integration demonstrates multi-database modernization scenarios

**Messaging and Integration**:

**IBM MQ**: Message queue integration (planned):
- Asynchronous messaging patterns replacing transient data queues
- Event-driven architectures for decoupling components
- Integration with cloud-native messaging services

**Amazon API Gateway**: API exposure for modernized services:
- RESTful API endpoints for credit card management functions
- Enables integration with web applications, mobile apps, partner systems
- API security through IAM, Cognito, or custom authorizers

**AWS Lambda**: Serverless compute for specific workloads:
- Batch job transformation to Lambda functions
- Event-driven processing for transaction posting, interest calculation
- Reduces infrastructure overhead for intermittent workloads

**Monitoring and Operations**:

**Amazon CloudWatch**: Monitoring, logging, and observability:
- Application logs from CICS regions and batch jobs
- Performance metrics (transaction rates, response times, error rates)
- Alarms for operational issues and SLA violations
- Integration approach: Log streaming from Micro Focus or application instrumentation

**AWS X-Ray**: Distributed tracing for microservices:
- Transaction flow visibility across refactored components
- Performance bottleneck identification
- Dependency mapping for complex workflows

## 3.8 Open Source Dependencies and Licensing

### 3.8.1 COBOL Copybooks as Data Contracts

**Copybook Library** (`app/cpy/` - 28 files):

**Record Layout Copybooks**: Define data structures for VSAM file records:
- `CVACT01Y.cpy` - Account Record (ACCOUNT-RECORD, 300 bytes)
- `CVACT02Y.cpy` - Card Record (CARD-RECORD, 150 bytes)
- `CVACT03Y.cpy` - Cross-Reference Record (XREF-RECORD, 50 bytes)
- `CVCUS01Y.cpy` / `CUSTREC.cpy` - Customer Record (CUSTOMER-RECORD, 500 bytes)
- `CVTRA01Y.cpy` - Transaction Category Balance (TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD, 50 bytes)
- `CVTRA02Y.cpy` - Disclosure Group (DIS-GROUP-RECORD, 50 bytes)
- `CVTRA03Y.cpy` - Transaction Type (TRAN-TYPE-RECORD, 60 bytes)
- `CVTRA04Y.cpy` - Transaction Category (TRAN-CAT-RECORD, 60 bytes)
- `CVTRA05Y.cpy` - Transaction Record (TRAN-RECORD, 350 bytes)
- `CVTRA06Y.cpy` - Daily Transaction (DALYTRAN-RECORD, 350 bytes)
- `CVTRA07Y.cpy` - Report Layout (report formatting structures)
- `CSUSR01Y.cpy` - User Security Record (SEC-USER-DATA, 80 bytes)

**Communication Area Copybooks**: Define inter-program communication structures:
- `COCOM01Y.cpy` - COMMAREA (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing user context (CDEMO-USER-ID, CDEMO-USER-TYPE), program routing (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), and functional context (CDEMO-CUST-ID, CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM)

**Menu Option Copybooks**: Define menu structures and navigation:
- `COMEN02Y.cpy` - Main Menu Options (10 options with program names)
- `COADM02Y.cpy` - Admin Menu Options (4 administrative functions)

**UI Component Copybooks**: Define screen elements and messages:
- `COTTL01Y.cpy` - Screen Titles (CCDA-TITLE01 "AWS Mainframe Modernization", CCDA-TITLE02 "CardDemo")
- `CSMSG01Y.cpy` - Common Messages (thank you messages, invalid key messages, PF key instructions)
- `CSMSG02Y.cpy` - ABEND Data (error condition reporting)

**Work Area Copybooks**: Define working storage structures:
- `CVCRD01Y.cpy` - Card Work Areas (CC-WORK-AREAS) containing attention identifier flags (CCARD-AID-ENTER, CCARD-AID-PF3, CCARD-AID-PF7, CCARD-AID-PF8)
- `CSDAT01Y.cpy` - Date/Time Working Storage (date conversion variables)

**Utility Copybooks**: Define reusable procedures:
- `CSUTLDPY.cpy` - Date Validation Procedure (date edit logic)
- `CSUTLDWY.cpy` - Date Edit Working Storage (date validation variables)
- `CSSETATY.cpy` - Screen Attribute Setting Procedure (BMS attribute manipulation)
- `CSSTRPFY.cpy` - PF Key Mapping Procedure (maps EIBAID to CCARD-AID flags)
- `CSLKPCDY.cpy` - Lookup Procedures (phone/state/zip validation lookups)

**BMS Map Copybooks** (`app/cpy-bms/` - 17 files): Generated by BMS assembly process:
- AI (Input) structures: Physical 3270 data stream layout with COMP PIC S9(4) length fields
- AO (Output) structures: REDEFINES overlays with attribute flags (C/P/H/V suffixes for Color/Protection/Highlighting/Validation)
- Examples: `COSGN00.CPY`, `COMEN01.CPY`, `COACTVW.CPY`, `COACTUP.CPY`, `COCRDLI.CPY`, `COCRDSL.CPY`, `COCRDUP.CPY`, `COTRN00.CPY`, `COTRN01.CPY`, `COTRN02.CPY`, `COBIL00.CPY`, `CORPT00.CPY`, `COUSR00.CPY`, `COUSR01.CPY`, `COUSR02.CPY`, `COUSR03.CPY`

**CICS System Copybooks**: IBM-provided standard copybooks:
- `DFHAID` - CICS Attention Identifier constants (DFHENTER, DFHPF1-DFHPF24, DFHCLEAR, DFHPA1, DFHPA2)
- `DFHBMSCA` - BMS Attribute constants (DFHRED, DFHGREEN, DFHBLUE, DFHYELLOW, DFHTURQ, DFHNEUTR, DFHBMPEM, DFHBMPSE, DFHUNPRO)

**Copybook Usage Pattern**: All COBOL programs use COPY statements to include copybooks at compile time:
```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY COCOM01Y.          *> Communication Area
COPY CVACT01Y.          *> Account Record Layout
COPY COACTVWI.          *> BMS Map Input Structure
COPY COACTVWO.          *> BMS Map Output Structure
COPY COTTL01Y.          *> Screen Titles
COPY CSMSG01Y.          *> Common Messages
```

This compile-time inclusion ensures consistency of data structures across all programs accessing shared files and communication areas.
